comments.author: meuk
comments.story_title: Systems Software Research is Irrelevant (2000) [pdf]
comments.why_zh: Muratori 关于操作系统复杂性和硬件多样性的吐槽
comments.quote_zh: Casey Murati 对此有过一段很精彩的吐槽
comments.text_zh: 我觉得问题在于现在的操作系统太复杂了。普通用户真正想要什么？我会说是文本编辑、做演示文稿、多媒体和浏览网页。这些听起来像是简单的事情，但文本编辑通常是在类似 Word 的格式里进行的，而据我所知，那种格式复杂得离谱。浏览网页也一样（简单的浏览器已经不存在了，很多浏览器用同样的后端来做渲染）。对于多媒体，USB 非常重要，而 USB 是个要正确使用极其复杂的格式。然后，多媒体有几十种编解码器和格式，每一种都有自己的怪癖和规范中的含糊之处（或者那些偏离规范、但如今已经常见到被视为理所当然的做法）。如果你的操作系统还要运行在不同的硬件上，情况就更糟了。我觉得这就是 Apple 总体上用户体验好得多的主要原因：他们只需要支持有限的硬件。Casey Murati 对此有过一段很精彩的吐槽：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I think the problem is that current OSes are too complicated. What does a common user really want? I'd say text editing, making presentations, multimedia, and browsing. While these sound like simple things, text editing usually happens in a Word-like format, which - from what I've heard - is ridiculously complex. The same thing holds for browsing (simple browsers don't exist anymore, and many use the same back-end for rendering). For multimedia, USB is very important, which is a very complicated format to use correctly. Then, there are tens of codecs and formats for multimedia, each with their own idiosyncrasies and ambiguities in the specs (or deviations from the spec that are so common that they are expected nowadays). The case is even worse when your OS is supposed to run on different hardware. I think this is the main reason that Apple, in general, has a much better UX: They only have to support a limited set of hardware. Casey Murati has a great rant about this: [VIDEO]

comments.author: loup-vaillant
comments.story_title: Zapcc – A caching C++ compiler based on clang
comments.why_zh: 引用以讨论软件膨胀以及为何需要这么多代码
comments.text_zh:
所以现在不仅项目需要维护，我们还得维护改动？对于“什么东西都永远没法完成”这种观念，我真是越来越受不了了。Bug？那只会是改动引入的那些，没别的。如果还剩下什么 bug，那只是因为还没人发现它们而已。有个维护者也改变不了这一点，只有使用才能暴露 bug。（当然，除非这位“维护者”的任务本来就是找 bug）。代码腐化？那只有在代码周围的环境发生变化时才是问题。Clang 是个编译器，它并不怎么在乎自己的环境。如果你说的是 Clang 内部可能产生影响的改动，那些完全在维护者的控制范围内。我们不该每打一个补丁就需要一个维护者。尤其是这个改动，似乎没有引入任何新功能。我猜它只是让 Clang 跑得更快。新的代码路径取代了旧的，所以应该不需要多出多少维护工作。

---

更广泛地说，我们应该抛弃“一切都应该永远维护下去”的观念。我们应该有能力写出正确的程序。我们应该有足够稳定的环境来保持这种正确性。而且我们首先就不该再相信我们需要这么多代码。别自欺欺人了，程序“需要维护”（这是“没写完”的委婉说法），主要是因为它们大得离谱。我们真的可以做得更好。
comments.text: So now not only projects have to be maintained, we also have to maintain changes ? I'm seriously getting sick at the notion that nothing can ever be finished. Bugs? That will be those introduced by the change, nothing more. If there is any bug left, that's only because nobody discovered them yet. Having a maintainer won't change that, only usage reveals bugs. (Unless of course the "maintainer" is instead tasked with finding bugs in the first place). Bit rot? That's only an issue when the environment around the code changes. Clang is a compiler , there's not much it cares about its environment. And if you're talking about changes within Clang that could have an effect, and those are well within the maintainer's control. We shouldn't need a maintainer for every patch. This change in particular doesn't seem to introduce any new feature. I'm guessing it only allows Clang to run faster. The new code path replaces the old, so it shouldn't require much more maintenance. --- More generally, we should do away with the notion that everything should be maintained, forever. We should be able to code correct programs. We should have environments stable enough to preserve that correctness. And we should stop believing we need so much code in the first place. Let's not kid ourselves, programs "require maintenance" (euphemism for "aren't finished"), mainly because they're so damn big. We can do better, really. [LINK] [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我碰巧读过不少 VPRI 的论文，并且在其中几个主题上有一些领域知识，或者认识具备这类领域知识的密友。顺便说一句，我收集的他们的链接在 [LINK]。这个目标很崇高；不过我不确定他们的研究是不是正确的道路。Alan Kay 那帮人的研究，最终成果往往很棒，但他们的实现通常更偏向原型验证，而不是生产环境。例如，GUI 创新很棒，而它用 Smalltalk 的实现显然是为了更快迭代，并不是要和一门生产级语言竞争（我们别展开这个争论，那是另一个兔子洞。HN 上有很多相关帖子）。但我觉得到目前为止，这些实现能得到宽容，是因为最终成果足够有未来感，足以让其他人随后用更面向生产的语言去实现，比如 GUI。然而在 VPRI 的语境下，目标并不是创造更有未来感的最终成果，而是用希望大幅更简洁的范式和 DSL 来重现已有成果。在这种情况下，实现本身才是我们应该审视的东西，而在我看来，他们有点不够格。例如： - 是的，Nile 能把抗锯齿逻辑缩减这么多，非常吸引人。但它能适应现实世界需求的变化吗？不清楚（而且 Nile 的论文还没发表，作者似乎忙着搞某个创业公司）。 - OMeta 解析器工具很酷，直到你 e
comments.text: I happened to have read many of VPRI’s papers and some domain expertise in a few of their topics, or know close friends with such domain expertise. Btw, my collection of their links are at [LINK] The goal is a noble one; though it's unclear to me if their research is the right way to go. Alan Kay's gang's research's end result are often great, but their implementations are usually more geared toward prototyping rather than production. For example, the GUI innovation is great, whereas its implementation using Smalltalk is clearly geared toward faster iteration and not meant to be as competitive as a production language (let's not enter into this debate as this is another rabbit hole. Plenty of other HN threads on this). But I think so far these implementations have gotten a pass because the end result is futuristic enough for someone else to come along and implement e.g. the GUI in more production-oriented languages. In the context of VPRI, however, the goal wasn't to create more futuristic end results, but to recreate existing result using hopefully drastically more concise paradigms and DSLs. In this case, the implementation itself is the thing we should examine, and imo they kinda fall short. For example: - Yes, it's very appealing that Nile can reduce the antialiasing logic by so much. comments.text: “In the 1980s with things like the Amiga computer, for example, every game was a boot disk. It booted into its own customized version of an operating system that ran what it needed to run to make its game work well and be performant and reliable. … We know that in the past, hardware that was very capable and very interesting made it so easy to create an operating system that literally everybody did it. Not a few people. Not even most people. But literally everybody.” – Casey Muratori in “The Thirty Million Line Problem” [VIDEO]
